clue.text: Put back bright coloured spot inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the word for spot sits within the colour word

parts.note: red is a bright colour
a spot is a place or location

explanation.surface: Someone restores a vivid splash of colour within a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spot' suggests a blemish of colour, but it means a location; 'inside' sets it within the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put back has been returned to its original position, a synonym.

clue.text: Commemorative meal?

parts.note: split the answer as RE plus a word for times gone by: a meal concerning bygone days would be commemorative

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: RE (about) plus PAST, so a meal 'about the past' sounds commemorative.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal word for a meal, read here as being about history.

clue.text: Miscreant making copper angry

parts.note: P stands for penny, a copper coin in Britain
irate means angry

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer infuriates a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is a penny, the British copper coin abbreviated P.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate is a sea robber, a kind of criminal or villain.

clue.text: Sound study but it may appear to be so caustic

indicators.note: may appear to be suggests the letters of the following words appear in a new form

explanation.surface: A remark that a science of hearing could seem bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may appear to be' rearranges SO CAUSTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Acoustics is the branch of physics concerned with how noise travels.

clue.text: Latest time for morning coffee

definitions.meaning: the last possible moment before a deadline
eleven o'clock in the morning, the traditional British hour for a coffee break called elevenses

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, mid-morning coffee is 'elevenses', taken around eleven o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the last moment, and literally it names eleven o'clock, the elevenses break.

clue.text: Two men — one benefactor

parts.note: Pat is a man's name
Ron is a second man's name, making the two men

explanation.surface: A pair of chaps are one generous supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two men' supplies two male names, PAT and RON.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron is a sponsor who gives financial support, a synonym of benefactor.

clue.text: An attempt to take people back

parts.note: a bash is an attempt, as in 'have a bash'

explanation.surface: Someone tries to win followers back again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take back' here means take aback, startle; 'have a bash' is British for 'have a go'.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash is to disconcert or embarrass, taking someone aback.

clue.text: Not looking forward to getting it?

definitions.text: Not looking forward to getting it?

parts.words: Not looking forward to getting it?
parts.note: sounds like dreading something, but describes a glance behind you, as in a car's mirror

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not looking forward' reads as reluctance; literally it means looking backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This view is what you see behind you, so you are looking the other way from ahead.

clue.text: Characteristic of the pure in spirit?

definitions.text: Characteristic of the pure in spirit?

parts.words: Characteristic of the pure in spirit?
parts.note: a spirit drunk undiluted is served neat, so being pure as liquor is its quality

explanation.walkthrough: 'pure in spirit' sounds holy, but spirits taken pure (no water) are neat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidiness is the usual sense, but here it is the quality of undiluted liquor.

clue.text: Left after breathing space, to study

indicators.note: after places the word for left following the small opening

parts.note: a pore is a tiny opening in the skin through which it breathes
over means left, as in remaining

explanation.surface: A person departed after taking a breather to do some revision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' is not L here but 'remaining', as in food left over; 'after' sets that word behind the breathing hole.
explanation.definitionFit: To pore over something is to examine it closely, an idiom for reading carefully.

clue.text: Girl is able to get first place

indicators.note: to get first places the verb for being able at the front

parts.note: can means is able
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman manages to win the top spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get first' puts CAN (is able) ahead of ADA.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada is a country, an example of a place on the map.

clue.text: Disliking the cut of the cloth?

definitions.text: Disliking the cut of the cloth?

parts.words: Disliking the cut of the cloth?
parts.note: the cloth means clergy, so disliking that profession, not a tailoring style

explanation.walkthrough: 'the cloth' is an idiom for the clergy, and 'the cut of someone's jib' for their manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against the church's priests and their influence fits disliking the clergy.

clue.text: Is satisfying to have had a meal aboard

annotationWithheld.why: Is satisfying to have had a meal aboard (5): ATE inside SS, but the only word for SS is 'aboard', which is also the container indicator, so one word does two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Is satisfying to have had a meal aboard

clue.text: Dine out at seaside resort north of Netherlands city

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order

parts.note: Hove is a seaside resort beside Brighton on England's south coast

explanation.surface: An invitation to eat at a coastal town above a Dutch city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DINE as EIND. HOVE is a resort town on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Eindhoven is a large city in the southern Netherlands, home of Philips.

clue.text: Car salesmen offering spare parts?

parts.note: people who supply goods to shops, and also the ignition component in an engine

explanation.walkthrough: A distributor is a part of a car's ignition; the setter plays on dealers who distribute.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who hand out goods to retailers are traders; the engine component shares the name.

clue.text: Because Una made her choice, to hold on to small daughter?

definitions.text: Because Una made her choice, to hold on to small daughter?

indicators.note: to hold on to says the pair of words wrap round the abbreviation

parts.note: opted means made a choice
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Una chose to keep her little girl rather than give her up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold on to' sets D within UNA OPTED. A road or child 'unadopted' is one nobody has taken on; here Una chose to keep her girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A child not taken in by new parents is not legally made someone else's, which is what Una's choice ensures.

clue.text: Noisy aircraft 'coming from the south

indicators.note: coming from puts the compass letter before the plane in this down clue

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south
the Trident was a British airliner of the 1960s and 70s

explanation.surface: A loud plane arrives from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming from' places S ahead of TRIDENT, a Hawker Siddeley airliner.
explanation.definitionFit: Strident means loud and harsh-sounding, a synonym.

clue.text: Unsteady runner takes time over this changeover

parts.note: a ski is a runner on snow, as on a sledge

indicators.note: changeover tells us the small word nearby is rearranged

explanation.surface: A wobbly athlete is slow at the baton exchange in a relay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' suggests an athlete, but a ski runs over snow; 'changeover' rearranges the small word this to give TISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Skittish means nervous or flighty, so unreliable and unstable.

clue.text: Goes ahead with illegal roof-stripping?

definitions.meaning: moves into first place in a race
stealing the metal sheeting off a roof

explanation.walkthrough: Lead sheeting on church roofs is a common target for metal thieves in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means moving in front, and literally it is stealing a roof's metal.

clue.text: Clothing I treat roughly

indicators.note: roughly signals the letters are handled loosely and rearranged

explanation.surface: A confession of mishandling garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' rearranges I TREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Attire is dress or garments, a synonym.

clue.text: Opera star of singular spirit

parts.note: one means singular, a single thing
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A diva with a unique character.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugene Onegin is Tchaikovsky's opera, named for its title character.
explanation.definitionFit: The title role of Tchaikovsky's opera is the lead character, its star.

clue.text: His plots somehow ring true from the start, I find

indicators.note: from the start puts the single letter at the front
somehow signals the words before it are mixed up

explanation.surface: A novelist's stories seem plausible from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges RING TRUE; 'from the start' puts I in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A schemer is a person who devises plots, so his plots define him.

clue.text: Once natural to put one on the spot and another inside.

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: inside places the second single within the word for spot

parts.note: a dot is a spot
another one, again I as the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Instructions for marking a place twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'natural' was an old word for a simpleton; 'on' places I above DOT, and 'inside' puts another I in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural was once a term for a fool born simple-minded, an archaic synonym.

clue.text: Much of the time half a score's property

parts.note: a possessive 's shows belonging, expressed by the word of
a score is twenty, so half is ten

explanation.surface: Ten gets most of the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a score's property' is something belonging to a score, so 'of' a score.
explanation.definitionFit: Often means frequently, on many occasions.

clue.text: Team in trouble about drink

indicators.note: in places the team within the word for trouble
about turns the word for trouble round

parts.note: rile means to trouble or annoy
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A side in crisis turns to alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the word for trouble round to give ELIR; 'in' then sets the team within it.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a magical potion, a drink to cure all ills.

clue.text: Athletic club's about to object, with scorn

indicators.note: about turns the club's letters round

parts.note: AC is athletic club, with 's adding S
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: An athletics club is going to protest disdainfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the club's letters round to give SCA; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Scathing means bitterly critical, full of contempt.

clue.text: Thai cook putting it in this place

indicators.note: in places the word it within the rearranged letters
to cook something is to fiddle it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Thai chef inserting something in a dish here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' rearranges the nationality to TAHI; 'in' then sets IT inside, with 'putting' just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is an island in French Polynesia, an example of a place.

clue.text: Fractured leg bound to result from attack with this weapon

indicators.note: fractured means broken, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken leg may result from being hit with a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fractured' rearranges LEG BOUND.
explanation.definitionFit: A bludgeon is a heavy club, a weapon for striking.
